N is connected to the central carbon on the left/below, and the central carbon is then connected to the upper acyl fragment R-C(=O)- and to a lower carbon chain bearing R1, H, and leading to the lower acyl R2-C(=O)-. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning count: According to the specified method, there are 6 heavy-atom–heavy-atom bonds within the pyridinium ring. The non-ring part is counted in order as: N-central carbon 1; central carbon-upper carbonyl carbon 1; upper C=O 1; upper carbonyl carbon-R 1; central carbon-lower carbon 1; lower carbon-R1 1; lower carbon-methylene/chain carbon 1; chain carbon-lower carbonyl carbon 1; lower C=O 1; lower carbonyl carbon-R2 1. The non-ring part totals 10. Exclude C-H bonds, and ignore Br− and arrows. Total = 6+10=16.

raw_record.question_text:
In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: Partition the structure into components visible in the image. Count the six heavy-heavy bonds around the pyridinium ring. Then count the non-ring heavy-heavy bonds: N to central carbon; central carbon to upper carbonyl carbon; upper C=O; upper carbonyl carbon to R; central carbon to lower carbon; lower carbon to R1; lower carbon to the methylene/chain carbon; that chain carbon to lower carbonyl carbon; lower C=O; lower carbonyl carbon to R2. Exclude the lower carbon-H bond and ignore arrows and Br−. Sum the ring count and side-chain/carbonyl counts to obtain the total.
